properties.label: opcodes
properties.text: For an account already in live state, verify that after SELFDESTRUCT zeroes its balance a subsequent credit of v!=0 makes the queried balance exactly v and never 0, so no client prunes or re-empties the re-funded account.
properties.assertion: a in L.live && v != 0 => bal(setBal(setBal(L,a,0),a,bal+v), a) == v && != 0

audit_packet.guarantee: Zeroing an account's balance (the SELFDESTRUCT destroy step) is not a sticky or terminal state: for a live account a, a following credit of a nonzero amount v yields a balance that reads back as exactly v, hence nonzero, so every client must observe the re-funded account as existing and funded rather than as a destroyed/zero account.
preconditions: Account a is a member of the live account list (ha : a in L.live) before both the zeroing write and the credit write; the packet says nothing about accounts absent from live state.
The credited amount is nonzero (hv : v != 0); a zero-value credit is outside the guarantee.
The live list is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct) and balance lookup is the single accessor Ledger.bal, so there is exactly one balance cell for a and no shadow copy can be read instead.
Reads use the same balance accessor after the writes as the invariant does (bal of the updated ledger), i.e. the post-credit query is not served from the pre-destroy ledger value.

supporting_facts.claim: Root guarantee: for live a and v != 0, the balance of a after zeroing then crediting v is not 0.
supporting_facts.check: Drive the destroy path so the balance of a live account a is set to 0, then apply a credit of v != 0 to the same account, then read the balance of a through the normal balance accessor.
supporting_facts.expected: The read returns a nonzero balance; the account is treated as present and funded by every client.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The read returns 0, or the account is reported as destroyed/nonexistent/pruned, or the credit is discarded because a destroy marker for a is set.

supporting_facts.claim: Stronger exact form: the post-zero, post-credit balance of a equals exactly v (not merely nonzero).
supporting_facts.check: Compare the balance of a after the zero-then-credit sequence against the credited amount v, for several distinct v values and several distinct pre-destroy balances of a.
supporting_facts.expected: balance(a) == v exactly, independent of the balance a held before the zeroing write.
supporting_facts.flag_if: balance(a) != v: any residue of the pre-destroy balance surviving (balance == old + v), any truncation, any saturation, or any partial credit.

supporting_facts.claim: Destroy guard: immediately after the zeroing write, the balance of a is exactly 0.
supporting_facts.check: Read the balance of a right after the zeroing write and before any credit.
supporting_facts.flag_if: balance(a) != 0 after the zeroing write, i.e. the destroy step leaves any residual balance visible to a later read.

supporting_facts.claim: Write-then-read agreement: for a live account, setting the balance of a to any value v and reading a back yields exactly v.
supporting_facts.check: For a live account a, write an arbitrary balance v (including 0, small, and large values) and immediately read the balance of a.
supporting_facts.expected: The read returns exactly the value just written, for every v including 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The read returns a stale, defaulted, clamped, or otherwise transformed value instead of the value written.

supporting_facts.claim: Underlying point-update primitive: the pointwise balance update at a returns exactly the written value at a, regardless of the prior value at a.
supporting_facts.check: Exercise the primitive balance-update path used by both the zeroing write and the credit write; write v at a and read a, over a matrix of prior balances (0, nonzero, max).
supporting_facts.expected: The read at a is exactly v in every case; the prior balance at a has no influence on the result.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The primitive's result depends on the prior balance at a, or the update is skipped/no-oped for particular prior values such as 0.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm that both the zeroing write and the credit write are applied to an account that is in the live account list, and that the live-membership precondition is actually established (not assumed) at each call site of the balance update.
derived_obligations.expected: Both writes are performed only against a live account a, and membership of a is established before the zeroing write and still holds for the credit write.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Either write is applied without establishing live membership, or the zeroing write removes a from the live list so the subsequent credit targets an account no longer covered by the invariant.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the nonzero-amount side condition is respected: the credit path must distinguish v == 0 from v != 0 and must not treat a nonzero credit as a no-op.
derived_obligations.expected: A credit with v != 0 always reaches the balance update; only v == 0 is outside the guarantee.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A nonzero credit is skipped, dropped, or folded into a no-op branch (e.g. a destroyed/zero-balance short circuit), or v is truncated to 0 before the write.

derived_obligations.check: Consensus-divergence probe: run the exact zero-then-credit-of-v!=0 sequence on the same account across every consensus-relevant execution path and confirm all agree on the final balance and on the account's existence.
derived_obligations.expected: All paths agree that balance(a) == v != 0 and that a exists; the resulting state commitment is identical everywhere.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any path yields 0 / account-absent while another yields v, i.e. a remotely reachable state-root disagreement from a single transaction that destroys then re-funds an account.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm that the destroy-time zeroing and the later credit both go through the single balance cell for a, given the live list is duplicate-free.
derived_obligations.expected: There is exactly one balance entry for a; the credit updates the same entry the zeroing write cleared, and the read observes that entry.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicate or shadow entries for a exist so that the credit updates one entry while the read observes another still holding 0.

audit_packet.derivation: L004 establishes that the pointwise balance update writes exactly the given value at the target account; L002 lifts this to the balance setter for a live account (read-back equals value written, for any value including 0). L003 instantiates that at value 0 to give the destroy guard: right after the zeroing write, balance(a) == 0. L001 chains L003 and L002: the credit writes balance(a) + v where balance(a) is 0 by L003, so the read-back after the credit is exactly v. The root theorem (FACT-1) then applies the nonzero side condition v != 0 to conclude the final balance is not 0. The audit therefore checks the whole chain (exact zeroing, exact write-back, exact final value v) rather than only the weak nonzero endpoint, because a client that keeps the pre-destroy residue or drops the credit still satisfies 'nonzero' or 'zero' respectively while diverging on the state root.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq A] (L : EthTotal.Ledger A) (a : A) (ha : List.instMembership.mem L.live a) (v : Nat),
  Eq (((L.setBal a 0 ha).setBal a (instHAdd.hAdd ((L.setBal a 0 ha).bal a) v) ha).bal a) v
x_proof_closure.conclusion: Eq (((L.setBal a 0 ha).setBal a (instHAdd.hAdd ((L.setBal a 0 ha).bal a) v) ha).bal a) v

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq A] (L : EthTotal.Ledger A) (a : A) (v : Nat) (ha : List.instMembership.mem L.live a),
  Eq ((L.setBal a v ha).bal a) v
x_proof_closure.conclusion: Eq ((L.setBal a v ha).bal a) v

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq A] (L : EthTotal.Ledger A) (a : A) (ha : List.instMembership.mem L.live a),
  Eq ((L.setBal a 0 ha).bal a) 0

∀ {A : Type u} (L : EthTotal.Ledger A) (a : A) (dec : (b : A) → Decidable (Eq b a)) (v : Nat)
  (ha : List.instMembership.mem L.live a), Eq ((L.setBalOfPoint a dec v ha).bal a) v
x_proof_closure.conclusion: Eq ((L.setBalOfPoint a dec v ha).bal a) v
